title: Org Memory · The next session should know why
detail: Synthetic scenario · Real FalkorDB queries and tests · Separate local clients · Deterministic policy
speech: Org Memory helps a new coding session use what a teammate already discovered. This demonstration uses synthetic data, a real Falkor database, and actual test execution.

title: 1 / Follow the connection to an earlier discovery
detail: authentication.ts → previous investigation → mobile-client fact, with the source attached
speech: The request is to simplify authentication. An earlier investigation found that mobile checkout still needs legacy tokens. Falkor follows the relationship through past work and returns the fact with its source.

title: 2 / Inspect the query executed for this request
detail: Actual parameterized Cypher, returned row counts and measured timings
speech: The inspector exposes the Cypher actually executed during this request, including parameters, returned rows, and timings. The graph supplies the relationship path.

title: 3 / Direct-only retrieval misses this connection
detail: Disable expansion: 0 eligible memories. Enable it: the related discovery becomes available.
speech: With graph expansion disabled, this scenario returns no direct result. Following the connection through the earlier investigation brings back the relevant discovery.

title: 4 / Use the memory to choose and execute a check
detail: Removal fails · Compatibility-preserving simplification passes all 4 tests
speech: The bounded demo policy uses the retrieved fact to select a compatibility test. Removing legacy parsing fails. A real simplification that preserves compatibility passes all four tests. These outputs come from local test processes.

title: 5 / New evidence retires the old constraint
detail: Migration evidence supersedes the requirement; only the replacement fact is recalled.
speech: When new migration evidence is published, the old requirement is explicitly superseded. The next request returns the replacement fact, while retired nodes remain in the graph.

title: 6 / Alice records a discovery for her team
detail: Authenticated team graph · Each client has a separate key, workspace and hook state
speech: Now we switch to authenticated team clients. Alice and Bob have separate keys, workspaces, and hook state. Alice publishes the earlier discovery into their shared team graph.

title: 7 / Bob recalls Alice’s discoveries
detail: Different API key · Same organization and repository · 2 memories fetched from FalkorDB
speech: Bob uses his own credential to make a real request. He retrieves Alice's two memories, including the source and relationship path. They share organization memory rather than a local file.

title: 8 / Bob checks and contributes another fact
detail: Actual fixture tests run before Bob publishes F-bob-opt-out
speech: Bob runs the compatibility tests and records an additional observation about explicitly disabling legacy parsing. His publication preserves the earlier team knowledge.

title: 9 / Alice receives Bob’s new discovery
detail: 3 memories returned, including Bob’s fact; earlier evidence remains available
speech: Alice now retrieves three memories through her own key. Bob's new fact is available alongside the original discoveries, with its own source reference.

title: 10 / A different organization gets a separate graph
detail: Same repository slug · Different organization · 0 shared-team memories
speech: A third client uses the same repository name but belongs to another organization. Its separate graph returns zero memories from the shared team scenario.

title: 11 / Verify both hooks, sharing and permissions
detail: Actual CLI verification · Bidirectional hook delivery · Same-session exclusion · HTTP 403 checks
speech: The complete verification also runs each client's actual hook process with synthetic events. It checks both directions of delivery, same-session exclusion, and permission failures. This is a local prototype with a deterministic policy, not a recorded live Claude task.

title: Shared discoveries. Relevant context. Inspectable evidence.
detail: Reproduce locally: npm run demo:verify and npm run demo:users
speech: The repository includes local setup, reproducible verification commands, query traces, and test results. Org Memory carries useful discoveries into the next session, with the evidence attached.
